title: Separable-closure Cech coordinates for continuous coefficient modules
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $k^s/k$ be a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure]. Put $G_k=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its Krull topology. The morphism $v:\operatorname{Spec}k^s\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a covering in the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Its $(q+1)$-fold fibre product, for every integer $q\geq0$, identifies over $\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ with $\operatorname{Spec}k^s\times G_k^q$, where the latter means the inverse limit of the finite disjoint unions indexed by finite quotients of $G_k^q$. The face maps are those of the usual group Cech nerve, with the convention that the descent cocycle equation is $c(gh)=c(g)c(h)$.

Let $A$ be any nonarchimedean normed field, with its metric topology, and put $R_{A,T}=p_T^*\underline A$, $\underline A(S)=C(S,A)$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Then
$$\Gamma((\operatorname{Spec}k^s)^{q+1}_{/k},R_A)=C(G_k^q,A)$$
canonically, compatibly with face maps and continuous field homomorphisms. On $(\operatorname{Spec}k^s)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ every lisse $R_A$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module, sk-def-sfb-module-objects] is isomorphic to $R_A^{\oplus n}$ for some finite $n\geq0$. Moreover
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{R_A}(R_A^{\oplus n},R_A^{\oplus m})=M_{m\times n}(A)$$
by constant matrices, including $m=0$ or $n=0$. For a continuous field map $A\to B$, scalar extension on these free modules and on the displayed Cech rings is entrywise postcomposition, using ordinary internal module scalar extension [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Neither completeness nor algebraic closedness of the coefficient field $A$ is required.

source.place: Section 4.2, Lemma 4.2.12 (continuous-function sheaves), Section 7.3, Lemma 7.3.9 over a field, and the generic-field observation in Lemma 7.4.10, p. 71; agent expansion of the separable-closure Cech calculation. Also Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach, Example 3.1, p. 6.

proof.text: Write $\Omega=k^s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois], $\Omega/k$ is Galois. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-in-finite-galois-subextension], every finite subset lies in a finite Galois intermediate field $E$. Thus these fields form a nonempty directed set (include $k$, and apply the same assertion to finite generating sets of two fields), and their union is $\Omega$. The finite separable stages are finite etale by [lem-kun-algebraic-separable-smooth]. Hence $k\to\Omega$ is ind-etale, so weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. It is faithfully flat by [def-pd-separable-closure]. Both spectra are affine and the unique point is covered, so the singleton $v$ is a covering by the affine-open criterion of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

source.place: Example 4.1.4 and Definition 4.1.1; Stacks fields.tex Tags 0BMG (lemma-normal-closure-inside-normal), 0BU2 (lemma-infinite-galois-limit)

proof.text:
For a finite Galois $E/k$ inside $\Omega$, put $Q_E=\operatorname{Gal}(E/k)$. The algebra isomorphism in [lem-exc-finite-galois-tensor-decomposition](1), base changed along $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ in its first factor, gives $\Omega\otimes_k E\cong\Omega^{Q_E}$, with $a\otimes b\mapsto(a\sigma(b))_\sigma$. Here base change and the finite product identification are direct consequences of the tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]: apply a map to each coordinate and use the finitely many coordinate idempotents for its inverse. Iterating gives $\Omega\otimes_k E^{\otimes_k q}\cong\Omega^{Q_E^q}$. Reindex by successive increments: its coordinate at $(g_1,\ldots,g_q)$ is
$$a_0\otimes\cdots\otimes a_q\longmapsto a_0\,g_1(a_1)\,(g_1g_2)(a_2)\cdots(g_1\cdots g_q)(a_q).$$
For $q=0$ this is the identity of $\Omega$. Restriction from $E'$ to $E$ makes these maps compatible, as is seen by this formula on each pure tensor.

source.place: Tag 03SF, section-finite-etale-under-galois; tensor formula of the cited node; explicit iterated base change and incremental reindexing

proof.text: Pass to the directed union of the fields $E$ simultaneously in all $q$ variable factors. Tensor commutes with these colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits]; the diagonal system suffices since any finite list of stages has a common upper bound. Consequently the coordinate ring of the $(q+1)$-fold fibre product is $\varinjlim_E\Omega^{Q_E^q}$. The fibre product of affine spectra over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the spectrum of the tensor product by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] (with the projections of [def-pc-fibre-product]), applied $q$ times, and the multiplication of the tensor ring is that of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Taking spectra converts this colimit into the inverse limit of the finite disjoint unions by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit]. Finally [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit] identifies $G_k$ with $\varprojlim_E Q_E$ as a topological group, so this is precisely $(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)[G_k^q]$ in the sense of [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. One can use these quotients to compute that object: a continuous map from $G_k^q$ to a finite discrete set is constant on a finite cover by cylinder neighbourhoods; a common upper bound of their finitely many stages makes it factor through $Q_E^q$. Thus these finite quotients refine every finite continuous quotient, as required for the inverse-limit description.

source.place: Tag 0BU2, lemma-infinite-galois-limit; algebra.tex Tag 00DD, lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits; limits.tex Tag 01YW, lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit

proof.text: In the coordinates of steps 2–3 the vertices are $x,xg_1,xg_1g_2,\ldots,xg_1\cdots g_q$, where $xg$ means the map induced by $a\mapsto g(a)$ at the first geometric vertex. Omitting vertex $0$ changes the base vertex to $xg_1$ and leaves increments $(g_2,\ldots,g_q)$; omitting an interior vertex $i$ replaces $(g_i,g_{i+1})$ by $g_ig_{i+1}$; omitting the last drops $g_q$. Repeating a vertex inserts $1$. These formulas follow by substituting into the pure-tensor formula, so hold at every finite stage and at the limit. This fixes the convention: a descent identification from vertex 1 to vertex 0 has on a triple the equation $c(g)c(h)=c(gh)$.

source.place: Agent coordinate calculation expanding the field Cech nerve; compare Section 7.4 monodromy conventions

proof.text: Write $W_q$ for the $(q+1)$-fold fibre product, an object of $(\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\mathrm{proet}}$. By steps 2–3, $W_q=\operatorname{Spec}\varinjlim_E\Omega^{Q_E^q}$, and this colimit is $LC(G_k^q,\Omega)$: a locally constant function on $G_k^q$ factors through some $Q_E^q$ by the cylinder argument of step 3. The coefficient $A$ is totally disconnected, because distinct points are separated by complementary ultrametric balls (no completeness is used). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-continuous-realization], applied on $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$, identifies the ring sheaf $R_{A,k}=p_k^*\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] with $U\mapsto C(|U|,A)$, naturally in $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum], with $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ a point, $|W_q|=G_k^q$, the component of a stage $Q_E^q$ being the image under the projection. Thus $\Gamma(W_q,R_{A,k})=C(G_k^q,A)$ as rings, and for $q=0$ this is $C(*,A)=A$. Every face and degeneracy is a morphism of the site, so by naturality it acts by precomposition with its map of underlying spaces. By the pure-tensor formula of step 4 this is the increment map; the automorphism $\operatorname{Spec}g_1$ of the geometric vertex in $d_0$ is the identity of the one-point space $|\operatorname{Spec}\Omega|$, so moving the vertex has trivial action on $A$. For the coefficient ring on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ used in steps 6–10: [det-pe-condensed-point-coefficients], applied to the separably closed field $\Omega$ and the condensed ring $\underline A$, gives $\Gamma(\Omega[S],R_{A,\Omega})=C(S,A)$ naturally in profinite $S$, in particular $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,R_{A,\Omega})=A$; and [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp] for $v$ is the monoidal identification $v^*R_{A,k}\cong R_{A,\Omega}$ of ring objects.

source.place: Example 3.1, p. 6; Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 4.2.12; blueprint geometric-point coefficient evaluation

proof.text: The one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is w-contractible in [det-pe-wlocal-strict-contractible]: its sole point is closed, its component space is the one-point extremally disconnected profinite space, and its local ring is $\Omega$. This field is strictly henselian under [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]: its maximal ideal is zero, so the idempotent lifting condition for every finite algebra is the identity, and its residue field $\Omega$ is separably closed. Apply [det-pe-wcb-clopen-partition] to a lisse trivializing covering from [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. A finite clopen partition of this nonempty one-point scheme has exactly one nonempty member, namely the whole scheme. The supplied arrow into one member of the covering is therefore a section $s$ of that covering arrow $u$.

source.place: Section 2.4, w-contractibility criterion; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 0982, lemma-w-local-strictly-henselian-extremally-disconnected; blueprint det-pe-wcb-clopen-partition proof

proof.text: Let $u:U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ be the covering member of step 6 with its section $s$. Lisseness gives an isomorphism of $R_A|_{U}$-modules $L|_U\cong(R_A|_U)^{\oplus n}$ on the localization at $U$ in the sense of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; module objects are compared with sectionwise module sheaves, with the same sections and restrictions, by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. The section $s$ is a morphism of $(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)_{\mathrm{proet}}$, since $u\circ s=1$. By the relocalization clause of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], restricting along $s$ carries $L|_U$ to $L|_{\operatorname{Spec}\Omega}$ and $R_A|_U$ to $R_A|_{\operatorname{Spec}\Omega}$, sectionwise the identity, and carries the isomorphism to an isomorphism. Since $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is the final object of its own site, the localization at it is the whole site and these restrictions are $L$ and $R_A$. Finite direct sums of sheaves of modules are computed sectionwise, so restriction keeps them. Therefore $L\cong R_{A,\Omega}^{\oplus n}$, including $n=0$, with no condition on $A$ beyond those in the statement.

source.place: Agent restriction-of-a-trivialization argument along a section of a w-contractible covering; same geometric argument as Example 7.3.5 over a field

proof.text: Compute maps using the sectionwise module category equivalent to internal modules by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]; the size and sheafification conventions are those of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. A map $R_A^{\oplus n}\to R_A^{\oplus m}$ is determined by the images of its $n$ global standard basis sections. Its image on any object sends $(a_j)_j$ to $\sum_j a_j\,s_j|_U$, by linearity and restriction compatibility. Conversely this formula defines a module morphism for every tuple of global sections $s_j\in\Gamma(\Omega,R_A^{\oplus m})$. Finite sums of module sheaves are also finite products, sectionwise, so step 5 at $q=0$ identifies this group with $(A^m)^n=M_{m\times n}(A)$. Composition is matrix multiplication by the same formula. If $n=0$ there are no columns; if $m=0$ every column is zero. In either case both sides are singleton zero groups.

source.place: Example 3.1; elementary finite-free module calculation using the section-action equivalence

proof.text: For a continuous field map $\varphi:A\to B$, [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map] gives the coefficient morphism $\varphi_*:f\mapsto\varphi\circ f$ on every profinite $S$, hence the ring map $p_k^*\varphi_*:R_{A,k}\to R_{B,k}$ by the functoriality of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Under the realization isomorphisms of step 5 for $A$ and for $B$, it is postcomposition $f\mapsto\varphi\circ f$ on $C(|U|,-)$: both composites are ring-sheaf maps out of $p_k^*\underline A$ whose adjoints at each profinite test object send $f\in C(S,A)$ to $\varphi\circ f$ composed with the projection $|X[S]|\to S$, and [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-continuous-realization] characterizes its isomorphism by these adjoint equations. So on each Cech ring $C(G_k^q,A)\to C(G_k^q,B)$ it is $f\mapsto\varphi\circ f$, and on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ global sections it is $\varphi:A\to B$. It commutes with a face with increment map $d$ because $(\varphi\circ f)\circ d=\varphi\circ(f\circ d)$; the same applies to degeneracies.

source.place: Example 3.1, functoriality in topological rings; blueprint def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map

proof.text: For the ordinary internal extension of scalars of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], the balanced map $R_B\otimes_{R_A}R_A\to R_B$ sends $b\otimes a$ to $b\varphi(a)$ and has inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$; the two compositions are identities by the balancing and unit relations. The same formulas on $n$ summands give $R_B\otimes_{R_A}R_A^{\oplus n}\cong R_B^{\oplus n}$ (the extension is a left adjoint and preserves finite sums). A matrix $T=(t_{ij})$ sends $1\otimes e_j$ to $\sum_i\varphi(t_{ij})e_i$, hence extends to the entrywise matrix $\varphi(T)$. On a Cech object the coefficient-unit morphism is exactly the ring map from step 9. These are sheaf tensor identities, established by the coequalizer universal property; they require no formula identifying tensor products of sections with sections of tensor products. For $n=0$ the extension preserves the zero object. No limit of Cauchy sequences, completion, or coefficient-algebraic-closure argument occurs in any step.

source.place: Example 3.1 and the ordinary internal coequalizer definition of scalar extension; agent explicit balanced-map calculation
